title: Characterization of Diamond-like Carbon Coatings under Extreme Service Conditions
content: 16MnCr5 steel is a popular material in industrial applications due to its mechanical strength, ductility, and heat treatment ability. Its composition of carbon, manganese, and chromium makes it suitable for wear-resistant components like gears, shafts, and camshafts. However, it has limitations under extreme conditions like repetitive movements or corrosive environments, reducing its performance and service life. To overcome these limitations, advanced coatings like diamond-like carbon (DLC) have been developed. DLC has a hybrid structure, featuring sp3 (diamond) and sp2 (graphite) carbon bonds, making it suitable for various industries [1].
